title: Tracing — Log Every Step, Inspect a Trajectory

content.goal: Add a trace recorder to atlas.py.
content.why: You cannot debug an agent from a stack trace — you must capture the full trajectory: every model call, tool call, and observation. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.1.)
content.verify: The file saves. A Trace holds an id and a list of spans — the same trace-and-span structure you know from microservice tracing.

content.goal: Record a span for every model call and every tool call inside run_agent.
content.why: A span per operation, nested under one trace, mirrors the trajectory — your most valuable debugging asset. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.2.)
content.code:
# Inside run_agent, create trace = Trace() at the start, then:
#   before each model call:  t0 = time.time()
#   after it: trace.span("model", model=MODEL, tokens=resp.usage.total_tokens,
#                        ms=round((time.time()-t0)*1000))
#   for each tool call: trace.span("tool", name=tc.function.name,
#                                  args=tc.function.arguments)
# Return (answer, trace) so callers can inspect it.
content.verify: run_agent now returns the answer AND a trace. Each model and tool operation is recorded with timing and payload.

content.goal: Run a task and inspect the recorded trajectory.
content.why: Inspecting a real trajectory is how you diagnose wrong tool choices, bad arguments, loops, and drift. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.2.)
content.verify: You see the answer plus a trace summary (trace_id, step count, tools used) and every span in order. You can literally read what ATLAS did, step by step.

content.goal: Record total tokens and cost signals for the whole run.
content.why: Cost per request belongs in your trace — agents can spike costs, and you alert on that. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 16, section 16.3.)
content.code:
# Sum tokens across model spans:
#   total_tokens = sum(s.get("tokens", 0) for s in trace.spans if s["kind"] == "model")
#   trace.span("run_total", total_tokens=total_tokens, steps=len(trace.spans))
# Print it so you can watch cost per run.
content.verify: The trace reports total tokens for the run. A multi-step or looping task visibly costs more — exactly the signal you would alert on in production.
content.troubleshoot: Never log secrets or personal data into a trace (Ch 16). Keep payloads to what you need for debugging.

content.why: The same trajectory you record for debugging is what you would monitor in production and mine for new eval cases.
content.verify: All true — every run produces a trace of spans; model and tool operations record timing, tokens, and payloads; you can inspect the full trajectory and total cost; no secrets are logged. Next unit adds guardrails and defends against a prompt-injection attempt.
